DIAGNOSIS READY: Porphyria Cutanea Tarda (PCT).

The combination of chronic pruritic rash on sun-exposed areas (face/upper body), sensory symptoms in the palms (often due to neuropathy or reflex sympathetic dystrophy secondary to liver failure), and a history of agricultural exposure to arsenic or liver stress is highly suggestive. The oral/genital ulcers I asked about are more typical of lichen planus or pemphigus, whereas PCT presents with skin fragility, blistering, and hypertrichosis. Given the discrepancy in your rash description versus the initial palm complaints, I suspect the palm symptoms are actually a manifestation of systemic copper overload or neuropathy associated with liver dysfunction.
